[package]
name = "bivvy"
version = "1.10.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.93"
description = "Interactive development environment setup automation"
license-file = "LICENSE"
repository = "https://github.com/bivvy-dev/bivvy"
keywords = ["cli", "setup", "development", "automation"]
categories = ["command-line-utilities", "development-tools"]

[dependencies]
# CLI framework
clap = { version = "4.5.56", features = ["derive", "env"] }

# Interactive prompts
dialoguer = "0.12.0"
console = "0.16.2"

# Progress indicators
indicatif = "0.18.3"

# Serialization
serde = { version = "1.0.228", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0.149"
schemars = { version = "1.2", features = ["derive"] }

# YAML parsing
serde_yaml = "0.9"

# YAML with source location tracking (for lint error reporting)
marked-yaml = "0.8.0"

# Error handling
anyhow = "1.0.100"
thiserror = "2.0.18"

# File system (none — directory discovery and glob matching are in src/sys.rs)

# Process execution (PATH lookup is in src/sys.rs)

# HTTP client (for remote templates)
reqwest = { version = "0.13.1", default-features = false, features = ["blocking", "json", "rustls"] }

# Time handling (for state)
chrono = { version = "0.4.43", features = ["serde"] }

# Hashing (for project identification)
sha2 = "0.11"
hex = "0.4.3"

input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fix cache corruption from concurrent tool installs

Cache writes used plain fs::write which is not atomic — concurrent
writers could produce torn content files or partial JSON metadata,
corrupting the cache. Readers hitting a half-written metadata file
would get deserialization errors.

Replace all cache file writes with atomic write-to-temp-then-rename.
Each writer uses a unique temp filename (PID + counter) so concurrent
operations never collide. Also eliminate TOCTOU races in load()
(exists-then-read) and remove() (exists-then-delete) by handling
NotFound inline. Route revalidation content writes through the store
so they get the same atomic treatment.
EOF
)"

[package]
name = "bivvy"
version = "1.10.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.93"
description = "Interactive development environment setup automation"
license-file = "LICENSE"
repository = "https://github.com/bivvy-dev/bivvy"
keywords = ["cli", "setup", "development", "automation"]
categories = ["command-line-utilities", "development-tools"]

[dependencies]
# CLI framework
clap = { version = "4.5.56", features = ["derive", "env"] }

# Interactive prompts
dialoguer = "0.12.0"
console = "0.16.2"

# Progress indicators
indicatif = "0.18.3"

# Serialization
serde = { version = "1.0.228", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0.149"
schemars = { version = "1.2", features = ["derive"] }

# YAML parsing
serde_yaml = "0.9"

# YAML with source location tracking (for lint error reporting)
marked-yaml = "0.8.0"

# Error handling
anyhow = "1.0.100"
thiserror = "2.0.18"

# File system (none — directory discovery and glob matching are in src/sys.rs)

# Process execution (PATH lookup is in src/sys.rs)

# HTTP client (for remote templates)
reqwest = { version = "0.13.1", default-features = false, features = ["blocking", "json", "rustls"] }

# Time handling (for state)
chrono = { version = "0.4.43", features = ["serde"] }

# Hashing (for project identification)
sha2 = "0.11"
hex = "0.4.3"

input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fix cache corruption from concurrent tool installs

Cache writes used plain fs::write which is not atomic — concurrent
writers could produce torn content files or partial JSON metadata,
corrupting the cache. Readers hitting a half-written metadata file
would get deserialization errors.

Replace all cache file writes with atomic write-to-temp-then-rename.
Each writer uses a unique temp filename (PID + counter) so concurrent
operations never collide. Also eliminate TOCTOU races in load()
(exists-then-read) and remove() (exists-then-delete) by handling
NotFound inline. Route revalidation content writes through the store
so they get the same atomic treatment.
EOF
)"

[package]
name = "bivvy"
version = "1.10.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.93"
description = "Interactive development environment setup automation"
license-file = "LICENSE"
repository = "https://github.com/bivvy-dev/bivvy"
keywords = ["cli", "setup", "development", "automation"]
categories = ["command-line-utilities", "development-tools"]

[dependencies]
# CLI framework
clap = { version = "4.5.56", features = ["derive", "env"] }

# Interactive prompts
dialoguer = "0.12.0"
console = "0.16.2"

# Progress indicators
indicatif = "0.18.3"

# Serialization
serde = { version = "1.0.228", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0.149"
schemars = { version = "1.2", features = ["derive"] }

# YAML parsing
serde_yaml = "0.9"

# YAML with source location tracking (for lint error reporting)
marked-yaml = "0.8.0"

# Error handling
anyhow = "1.0.100"
thiserror = "2.0.18"

# File system (none — directory discovery and glob matching are in src/sys.rs)

# Process execution (PATH lookup is in src/sys.rs)

# HTTP client (for remote templates)
reqwest = { version = "0.13.1", default-features = false, features = ["blocking", "json", "rustls"] }

# Time handling (for state)
chrono = { version = "0.4.43", features = ["serde"] }

# Hashing (for project identification)
sha2 = "0.11"
hex = "0.4.3"

input.command:

Fix cache corruption from concurrent tool installs

Cache writes used plain fs::write which is not atomic — concurrent
writers could produce torn content files or partial JSON metadata,
corrupting the cache. Readers hitting a half-written metadata file
would get deserialization errors.

Replace all cache file writes with atomic write-to-temp-then-rename.
Each writer uses a unique temp filename (PID + counter) so concurrent
operations never collide. Also eliminate TOCTOU races in load()
(exists-then-read) and remove() (exists-then-delete) by handling
NotFound inline. Route revalidation content writes through the store
so they get the same atomic treatment.
EOF
)"

[package]
name = "bivvy"
version = "1.10.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.93"
description = "Interactive development environment setup automation"
license-file = "LICENSE"
repository = "https://github.com/bivvy-dev/bivvy"
keywords = ["cli", "setup", "development", "automation"]
categories = ["command-line-utilities", "development-tools"]

[dependencies]
# CLI framework
clap = { version = "4.5.56", features = ["derive", "env"] }

# Interactive prompts
dialoguer = "0.12.0"
console = "0.16.2"

# Progress indicators
indicatif = "0.18.3"

# Serialization
serde = { version = "1.0.228", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0.149"
schemars = { version = "1.2", features = ["derive"] }

# YAML parsing
serde_yaml = "0.9"

# YAML with source location tracking (for lint error reporting)
marked-yaml = "0.8.0"

# Error handling
anyhow = "1.0.100"
thiserror = "2.0.18"

# File system (none — directory discovery and glob matching are in src/sys.rs)

# Process execution (PATH lookup is in src/sys.rs)

# HTTP client (for remote templates)
reqwest = { version = "0.13.1", default-features = false, features = ["blocking", "json", "rustls"] }

# Time handling (for state)
chrono = { version = "0.4.43", features = ["serde"] }

# Hashing (for project identification)
sha2 = "0.11"
hex = "0.4.3"

commit fdeda285ac77d0ef2ac123fa9599cabc96fb7c4a
Author: benchmark <benchmark@localhost>
Date:   Tue May 12 14:01:28 2026 -0600

    Fix cache corruption from concurrent tool installs
    
    Cache writes used plain fs::write which is not atomic — concurrent
    writers could produce torn content files or partial JSON metadata,
    corrupting the cache. Readers hitting a half-written metadata file
    would get deserialization errors.
    
    Replace all cache file writes with atomic write-to-temp-then-rename.
    Each writer uses a unique temp filename (PID + counter) so concurrent
    operations never collide. Also eliminate TOCTOU races in load()
    (exists-then-read) and remove() (exists-then-delete) by handling
    NotFound inline. Route revalidation content writes through the store
    so they get the same atomic treatment.

 src/cache/store.rs        | 207 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++------
